input.content:
You are an expert OOP programming teacher who creates coding challenges for a multiplayer game. You generate tasks that teach object-oriented programming concepts through hands-on coding.

RULES:
- Tasks should be solvable in 2-5 minutes
- Starter code should have clear TODOs marking what to fix
- The solution must be complete and runnable
- Validation patterns must be literal code fragments from the solution
- Keep code concise (under 30 lines)
- Keep tasks beginner-friendly and not too complex
- Generate DIFFERENT scenarios each time (not always Dog/Animal or BankAccount)
- Use creative class names like Vehicle/ElectricCar, Weapon/Sword, Shape/Hexagon, etc.
- Visible checks should be written as plain English specs
- Validation patterns should be exact code fragments from the solution
- CRITICAL: starter_code and solution_code MUST be properly formatted multi-line code. Use real newline characters for line breaks and spaces for indentation. NEVER put all code on a single line. Each statement should be on its own line.

Generate a encapsulation coding task in javascript.

Language syntax reference:
JavaScript OOP:
- Class: class Animal { constructor(name) { this.name = name; } speak() { return this.name; } }
- Inheritance: class Dog extends Animal { constructor(name) { super(name); } }
- Private: use #field syntax or closures. Use #balance for private fields.
- Polymorphism: override methods in subclass, no keyword needed

The task should teach the concept of encapsulation through a creative, original scenario (don't use Animal/Dog or BankAccount — pick something unique and fun).

IMPORTANT: Format all code (starter_code and solution_code) with proper line breaks and indentation. Each line of code must be on its own line. Do NOT compress code into a single line.

content.title: Protect the Magic Orb's Energy
content.prompt: You're building a mystical artifact, the `MagicOrb`. Its internal `#energy` level must be protected from direct external access, only allowing controlled modifications through its methods. Implement the `MagicOrb` class with a private `#energy` field and public methods to interact with it, ensuring energy never drops below zero.
visible_checks: The MagicOrb's energy can be increased using the `charge` method with a positive amount.
The MagicOrb's energy can be decreased using the `drain` method, but it will never fall below 0.
The internal energy level of the orb is protected and can only be accessed via the `getEnergyLevel` method.
